topic: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem: Fairness in a Necklace

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Intuition of Antipodes
lecture_lines: Imagine a sphere, like a globe.
Like Tokyo and the South Atlantic.
They are mirrors through the center.
Symmetry is built into our world.
animations: Display a sphere using a wireframe style, color #FFFFFF.
Plot two antipodal points P and -P on the sphere, label them #FF00FF.
Draw a line segment connecting P and -P passing through the center, color #00FFFF.
Flash the antipodal points with a color #FF0000 to emphasize their symmetry.
Rotate the sphere slowly to show the antipodal relationship from different angles.

sections.title: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem (The Core Concept)
lecture_lines: Any continuous function maps antipodes equally.
Consider temperature and pressure on Earth.
Two opposite points always match perfectly.
This theorem guarantees a fair solution.
animations: Display a sphere, mapping values to 2D plane with color #FFFFFF.
Place two antipodal points on the sphere, label them #00FF00.
Show these points moving to the same value in the 2D plane, color #FFFF00.
Highlight the mapping equality f(x) = f(-x) using colored labels.
Display the Borsuk-Ulam theorem text in center, color #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Transition: From Spheres to Necklaces
lecture_lines: Two thieves want a fair share.
Can we cut fairly with beads?
animations: Display a sphere flattening into a circle, color #00FFFF.
Represent necklace beads as colored points along the circle, #FF00FF.
Animate shifting beads to demonstrate cutting the necklace, color #FFFF00.

sections.title: Application: Solving the Necklace Problem
animations: Display two necklaces with k types of colored beads, #FF00FF.
Show partitioning the beads into two equitable sets, color #00FF00.
Display the fair division formula, highlighting key components in color #FFFF00.

sections.title: Conclusion: Why Symmetry Matters
animations: Display a balanced scale representing symmetry, color #00FFFF.
Show Borsuk-Ulam theorem text leading into the scale, color #FFFFFF.
Final visual summary: Fair division is mathematically inevitable, #FF00FF.
